title: Best Soundbars UK
short: TV soundbars compared for dialogue clarity, bass response and Dolby Atmos performance, from compact budget bars to full multi-speaker surround systems.
intro: A soundbar's real test is how it handles a genuine range of content, not a single demo clip. This guide compares soundbars tested by Expert Reviews across films, sports, TV shows and music, with 4K Blu-ray and Dolby Atmos content from Netflix, Amazon Prime Video and Disney+ used to test surround-sound performance at a range of volumes.

products.name: Beam (Gen 2)
products.best_for: Buyers who want the best all-round soundbar that can expand into a full system later
products.key_spec: 2.0 channel (5-channel audio processing), 11 speaker drivers, Dolby Atmos, HDMI eARC
products.summary: Expert Reviews' favourite soundbar overall, with a neat one-box design and top-notch five-channel audio from 11 speaker drivers. Dolby Atmos handling particularly impressed, with positional audio cues deftly directed around the soundstage, and its output can be expanded by adding a Sonos Sub or Era speakers, though it lacks DTS:X support and dedicated up-firing drivers.
pros: Phenomenal audio quality with Dolby Atmos
Neat, compact one-box design
Easily expandable with extra Sonos speakers
Well-balanced across stereo and big movie soundtracks

products.name: Stage Pro
products.best_for: Buyers who want an affordable bar that works equally well with a TV or PC
products.key_spec: 2.1 channel, 80W RMS, SuperWide mode, near- and far-field listening modes
products.summary: Expert Reviews' top budget pick, eminently affordable and flexible while still sounding great. SuperWide mode effectively expands the soundstage for multi-channel film content, and testers particularly enjoyed how dialogue integrated smartly with the robust bass from the included subwoofer, though there's no Night mode and it's not great for music.
pros: Very affordable
Hefty bass response for the price
Works well for both TVs and PCs/laptops
Clear dialogue integration with the subwoofer
cons: Not the best choice for music

products.name: HW-Q990F
products.best_for: Buyers who want the most immersive possible surround sound and have the space for it
products.key_spec: 11.1.4 channel, 756W total power, soundbar plus subwoofer and two rear speakers
products.summary: Expert Reviews found no soundbar does Dolby Atmos more immersively than this, creating a dome of sound convincing enough that testers genuinely felt in the middle of on-screen action. Height effects from Atmos and DTS:X were articulated superbly with expertly judged crossover to the powerful sub, and it performed impressively for music too, though it's a space-hungry multi-component system.
pros: Incredibly immersive surround sound
Superb height effects on Atmos and DTS:X
Excellent connectivity options
Impressive for music as well as film
cons: Sub needs adjustment when switching to music

products.name: AX5125H
products.best_for: Budget buyers who have room for rear speakers and a subwoofer
products.key_spec: 5.1.2 channel, 500W total power, dedicated centre channel, overhead height channels
products.summary: Expert Reviews called this astonishing value for money, with no other bar tested getting close to it under £300. A dedicated centre channel ensures crisp dialogue, overhead channels depict height effects on Atmos and DTS:X soundtracks, and rear channels create a strong sense of envelopment, well beyond the typical 2.1 or 3.1 setup at this price.
pros: Exceptional value with genuine 5.1.2 surround
Effective Dolby Atmos and DTS:X performance
Clear dialogue via dedicated centre channel
Strong sense of audio envelopment

products.name: Bravia Theatre Bar 9
products.best_for: Buyers who want a single unit that sounds like a multi-speaker system
products.key_spec: 7.0.2 channel, single enclosure, expandable with optional sub and rear speakers
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this creates such an expansive, engrossing soundstage that testers forgot the audio was coming from a single enclosure. The unusual 7.0.2 setup has no built-in subwoofer, but the other channels place audio precisely enough that it's impossible not to get lost in the action, and music is handled especially well, though upgrade accessories aren't cheap.
pros: Expansive soundstage from a single unit
Excellent for both films and music
Simple to upgrade with matched accessories
Attractive, space-efficient design

products.name: Smart Soundbar
products.best_for: Buyers who prioritise clear speech above all else
products.key_spec: 3.0.2 channel, AI Dialogue mode, Bose Open Ultra Earbuds integration
products.summary: Expert Reviews found no standalone soundbar tested reproduces speech in films and TV better than this, thanks to an AI Dialogue mode that recognises vocal moments and automatically pushes them forward in the mix. It did so remarkably well without upsetting overall balance, and it also handles Atmos and music effectively, though bass response is limited and there's no HDMI passthrough.
pros: Best-in-class dialogue clarity via AI Dialogue mode
Handles Dolby Atmos effectively
Works well with Bose headphones and earbuds
Good for both TV and music

products.name: Arc Ultra
products.best_for: Buyers already invested in, or planning to build, a Sonos multi-room system
products.key_spec: 9.1.4 channel, TruePlay room calibration, expandable with Sonos Sub and Era speakers
products.summary: Expert Reviews called this a 'triumph of audio hardware' on its own, with TruePlay room calibration ensuring optimal sound and noticeably improved bass and three-dimensionality over previous Sonos bars. It works brilliantly standalone, but pairs with the wider Sonos ecosystem for magnificent multi-room audio, though it has only one HDMI input and no DTS:X support.
pros: Top-notch multi-room functionality within the Sonos app
Excellent three-dimensional audio and height effects
Improved bass response over previous Sonos bars
TruePlay automatically calibrates for your room

products.name: HW-S800D
products.best_for: Buyers who need a bar that fits under a TV with minimal clearance
products.key_spec: 3.1.2 channel, ultra-slim 40mm profile, discrete subwoofer, SmartThings and Alexa built in
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this incredibly slender bar fits neatly beneath TVs with minimal clearance, unlike typically bulky immersive soundbars. Atmos soundtracks were articulated with an impressive sense of scale and clean height effects despite the slim profile, and testers were particularly taken by the mid-range reproduction, though it lacks DTS:X and has limited sonic envelopment.
pros: Ultra-slim design fits under most TVs
Surprisingly large, convincing soundstage
Clean height effects despite slim profile
Built-in Amazon Alexa and SmartThings control
cons: Limited sonic envelopment compared to bulkier systems

products.name: Ray
products.best_for: Buyers with a 32in or 43in TV who want a genuinely compact soundbar
products.key_spec: 2.0 channel, compact minimalist design, app-based room calibration
products.summary: Expert Reviews found the most affordable Sonos soundbar ideally suited to smaller televisions, compact enough not to look out of place beneath them, yet with sonic delivery that belies its size. Great tonal balance, punchy bass and crisp treble are helped by Sonos' app-based tuning to match your room's acoustics, though there's no voice control and no remote is included.
pros: Compact size suits smaller TVs
Surprisingly capable sound for its size
App-based room calibration
Affordable entry into the Sonos ecosystem

guide.q: What do the channel numbers (2.1, 5.1, 11.1.4) actually mean?
guide.a: The first number is front-facing channels, the second (after the first dot) is subwoofers, and a third number refers to up-firing height speakers. A 2.1 setup like the Sonos Ray here suits music and everyday TV, a 5.1 setup like the Hisense AX5125H gives true surround sound for movies, and a system like the Samsung HW-Q990F's 11.1.4 adds immersive 3D height effects on top.

guide.q: Do I need a separate subwoofer?
guide.a: A discrete subwoofer, like the ones bundled with the Hisense AX5125H or Samsung HW-Q990F here, gives richer, room-shaking bass than a soundbar's built-in woofer can typically manage. It's usually wireless so you can hide it out of sight, since bass frequencies aren't very directional and don't need to sit centrally.

guide.q: Is a Dolby Atmos soundbar worth paying more for?
guide.a: Atmos and DTS:X add height effects on top of standard surround sound, using up-firing speakers to bounce audio off your ceiling, which Expert Reviews found works best with the right ceiling height. Atmos soundbars tend to cost more and sometimes skip DTS:X support, which matters if you regularly watch Blu-rays that use DTS encoding rather than Dolby.

guide.q: What is HDMI eARC and why does it matter?
guide.a: HDMI eARC (enhanced audio return channel) lets a soundbar receive and play audio directly from your TV's own apps, like Netflix or BBC iPlayer, without a separate cable from the source device. It's also useful if you run out of HDMI inputs on the soundbar itself, since audio that would normally play through the TV speakers gets routed back to the bar instead.
